claims.text: Hugging Face's guide to caching describes the KV cache as stored key-value pairs from the attention layers of tokens already processed, reused for later tokens so they need not be recomputed.

checks.method: git: verbatim source at release tag
git: fresh read of exact lines at release tag
independent reviewer (strict mode)

claims.text: The same guide contrasts the two: without a cache every step recomputes all previous keys and values, while with a cache each step computes only the current token's.

checks.method: git: verbatim source at release tag
git: fresh read of exact lines at release tag
independent reviewer (strict mode)

claims.text: Hugging Face's caching guide writes attention as softmax(QKᵀ/√d_head) × V, where the query, key and value matrices are projections of the input with shape (batch, heads, tokens, d_head).

checks.method: git: verbatim source at release tag
git: fresh read of exact lines at release tag

claims.text: because of the causal mask a token cannot look at later tokens, so once processed its keys and values never change and can be cached and reused.

cut.text: Exact parameter counts of the released Llama 3.1 checkpoints
cut.reason: Not read from a primary source in this session. Like Part 1, the page uses the nominal 8 and 70 billion; the released checkpoints are slightly larger, so real weight bytes are a little higher.

cut.text: Llama 3.1 layer and head counts read from the official Hugging Face config.json files (meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B and -70B)
cut.reason: The repositories are gated and the files could not be fetched from this session. The same values come from Meta's own reference code and the Llama 3 paper, which agree.

cut.text: Llama 2 7B as a real multi-head (MHA) example
cut.reason: Meta's sku_list.py lists 8 key/value heads for Llama 2 7B, which conflicts with Llama 2 7B being multi-head. With primary sources in conflict, the page uses a hypothetical MHA variant of the 8B model instead.

cut.text: vLLM's exact per-block page size formula in kv_cache_interface.py
cut.reason: At v0.31.0 the formula is spread across generic state-size properties; paging is Part 4. The page uses the per-token formula from Meta's code and the vLLM paper.

cut.text: The exact non-KV memory vLLM reserves on an H100 for Llama 3.1 8B
cut.reason: vLLM measures it at startup and it varies with version, CUDA graphs and settings. The page uses 3 GB as a labelled stand-in.
